text: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them into complex UIs, screens, pages, and apps
quote: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.

text: Add React to an existing HTML page or stack and render interactive components anywhere on it without rewriting the project
quote: You don’t have to build your whole page in React. Add React to your existing HTML page, and render interactive React components anywhere on it.

text: Use as little or as much React as you need
quote: you can use as little or as much React as you need

text: Implement an entire route subtree, such as all pages under one path, fully in React while the rest of the site stays non-React
quote: you want to implement all routes starting with `example.com/some-app/` fully with React.

text: A page can use many separate React roots to add sprinkles of interactivity to different parts
quote: A page that uses "sprinkles" of React for parts of the page may have as many separate roots as needed.

text: Write UI markup with JSX, a JavaScript syntax extension
quote: This markup syntax is called JSX. It is a JavaScript syntax extension popularized by React.

text: Each component is a piece of UI that carries its own logic and appearance
quote: React apps are made out of *components*. A component is a piece of the UI (user interface) that has its own logic and appearance.

text: Use plain JavaScript constructs such as if statements for conditional content and array map() for lists
quote: Want to show some content conditionally? Use an `if` statement. Displaying a list? Try array `map()`.

text: Components receive data and return UI, and React updates the screen when new data arrives from an interaction
quote: React components receive data and return what should appear on the screen. You can pass them new data in response to an interaction, like when the user types into an input.

text: Build full-stack React apps using recommended frameworks such as Next.js or React Router
quote: To build an entire app with React, we recommend a full-stack React framework like Next.js or React Router.

text: Build truly native Android and iOS apps in React using React Native and Expo
quote: React Native and Expo let you build apps in React for Android, iOS, and more. They look and feel native because their UIs are truly native.

text: Render React on the server using Node
quote: React can also render on the server using Node and power mobile apps using React Native.

text: Stream HTML from the server while data is still being fetched, filling in content progressively before JavaScript loads
quote: On the server, React lets you start streaming HTML while you’re still fetching data, progressively filling in the remaining content before any JavaScript code loads.

text: Fetch data in async components that run on the server or at build time, in supporting frameworks
quote: Frameworks that implement it let you fetch data in asynchronous components that run on the server or even during the build.

text: Mark a module and its transitive dependencies as client code with the 'use client' directive
quote: Add 'use client' at the top of a file to mark the module and its transitive dependencies as client code.

text: Frameworks let you add server-side rendering per route when it makes sense
quote: these frameworks allow you to add server-side rendering on a per-route basis, when it makes sense for your use case.

text: Deploy React apps to a CDN or static host without a server
quote: These apps can be deployed to a CDN or static hosting service without a server.

text: createRoot displays React components inside a browser DOM node
quote: createRoot lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node.

text: hydrateRoot attaches React to existing HTML that was server-rendered by react-dom/server
quote: Call `hydrateRoot` to “attach” React to existing HTML that was already rendered by React in a server environment.

text: Root option onUncaughtError provides a callback for errors not caught by an Error Boundary
quote: onUncaughtError: Callback called when an error is thrown and not caught by an Error Boundary.

text: identifierPrefix avoids useId conflicts when a page has multiple roots
quote: identifierPrefix: A string prefix React uses for IDs generated by useId. Useful to avoid conflicts when using multiple roots on the same page.

text: Get full TypeScript support for React web by adding @types/react and @types/react-dom
quote: you can get full React Web support by adding @types/react and @types/react-dom to your project.

text: Provide TypeScript types for component props
quote: The key difference when working with a component is that you can provide types for your component's props.

text: React Developer Tools let you inspect components, edit props and state, and find performance problems
quote: Use React Developer Tools to inspect React components, edit props and state, and identify performance problems.

text: React Native DevTools is a built-in debugger that integrates React Developer Tools for React Native apps
quote: To inspect apps built with React Native, you can use React Native DevTools, the built-in debugger that deeply integrates React Developer Tools.

text: React Compiler automatically handles memoization at build time, removing the need for manual useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo
quote: React Compiler automatically optimizes your React application at build time... eliminating the need for manual useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo.

text: Install React Compiler as a Babel plugin devDependency
quote: Install React Compiler as a devDependency: npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler@latest

text: Adopt React Compiler incrementally, starting with specific parts of the codebase
quote: React Compiler can be adopted incrementally, allowing you to try it on specific parts of your codebase first.

text: Use Babel overrides to apply the compiler to different parts of the codebase
quote: Babel's `overrides` option lets you apply different plugins to different parts of your codebase.

text: Exclude individual components from compilation with the 'use no memo' directive
quote: Using the "use no memo" directive to exclude components

text: Run A/B tests that measure the real-world impact of compiler optimizations by controlling which code is compiled
quote: By controlling which parts of your code get compiled, you can also run A/B tests to measure the real-world impact of the compiler's optimizations.

text: The compiler safely skips optimizing code that might break the Rules of React instead of changing app behavior
quote: When it encounters code that might break these rules, it safely skips optimization rather than risk changing your app's behavior.

text: The compiler works with plain JavaScript and requires no code rewrites
quote: It works with plain JavaScript, and understands the Rules of React, so you don't need to rewrite any code to use it.

text: React Compiler supports React 17, 18, and 19
quote: React Compiler is designed to work best with React 19, but it also supports React 17 and 18.

text: Enable the compiler in Vite through the reactCompilerPreset in @vitejs/plugin-react 6.0.0 or later
quote: If you use Vite with version 6.0.0 or later of `@vitejs/plugin-react`, you can use the `reactCompilerPreset`

text: Compiler errors surface at build time and block compilation, separate from runtime behavior issues
quote: Compiler errors occur at build time and prevent your code from compiling... Runtime issues occur when compiled code behaves differently than expected.

text: eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules catch severe bugs early
quote: Make sure that you've enabled all the eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules for your project. They are essential and catch the most severe bugs early.

text: Try React in an online sandbox without installing anything
quote: You don't need to install anything to play with React. Try editing this sandbox!

text: Beginner tutorial builds a tic-tac-toe game and assumes no prior React knowledge
quote: You will build a small tic-tac-toe game during this tutorial. This tutorial does not assume any existing React knowledge.

text: Start a React app from scratch with a build tool such as Vite, Parcel, or Rsbuild
quote: The first step is to install a build tool like `vite`, `parcel`, or `rsbuild`.

text: Convert large amounts of existing HTML to JSX with an online converter
quote: If you have a lot of HTML to port to JSX, you can use an online converter.

text: Guidance on breaking a UI mockup into a named component hierarchy
quote: Start by drawing boxes around every component and subcomponent in the mockup and naming them.
